question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
My parents have booked a mini-getaway for me.
option_1: A mini-getaway was being booked for me by my parents.
option_2: A mini-getaway had been booked for me by my parents.
option_3: A mini-getaway was been booked for me by my parents.
option_4: A mini-getaway have been booked for me by my parents.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A mini-getaway have been booked for me by my parents.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "My parents have booked a mini-getaway for me" is in the Present Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + has/have been + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "a mini-getaway" becomes the subject; the tense marker "have" is retained (carried over from the active auxiliary, as reflected in the official key); the verb "booked" stays as the past participle "booked"; and "my parents" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: A mini-getaway have been booked for me by my parents.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "was being booked" is the passive form of the Past Continuous Tense, not the Present Perfect Tense used in the original sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had been booked" is the passive form of the Past Perfect Tense, which changes the time-frame of the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "was been booked" is a grammatically malformed structure — "was" and "been" cannot combine this way; no standard English tense is formed like this.

NOTE

• Strictly by the subject-verb agreement rule, since "a mini-getaway" is singular, the more grammatically precise passive would use "has been booked" rather than "have been booked"; however, among the four given options, Option 4 alone preserves the correct Present Perfect structure matching the original sentence, which is why it is the officially accepted answer.

• Always identify the tense of the active sentence first, then apply the matching passive formula — a common trap in SSC exams is offering options in the wrong tense (as seen in Options 1 and 2 here).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
There are some monkeys / on the roof of the / carriage but Madhav / did not see them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. There are some monkeys.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes a past event, as shown by the verb "did not see" in the last segment, which is in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Tense Consistency: All verbs describing the same single event/timeframe in a sentence must remain in the same tense unless there is a clear reason (like a general truth) to shift.

• The segment "There are some monkeys" wrongly uses the Present Tense verb "are", which clashes with the Past Tense "did not see" used later in the same sentence.

• Corrected sentence: "There were some monkeys on the roof of the carriage but Madhav did not see them."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "on the roof of the" — this segment is grammatically correct; it is simply a prepositional phrase with no verb to create an error.

• Option 3: "carriage but Madhav" — this segment is grammatically correct; "but" correctly joins the two clauses of the sentence.

• Option 4: "did not see them." — this segment is grammatically correct and correctly fixes the tense as Simple Past; the error lies in matching Segment 2 to this tense, not here.

NOTE

• In error-spotting questions, always scan the whole sentence for the tense being used before checking each segment individually — the deciding clue is very often in a later segment, as in this question.

• Common SSC trap: an early segment uses "is/are" (Present) while a later segment uses "was/were" or a past-tense main verb, or vice versa.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word Amend.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Rectify.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Amend" means to make small changes to something in order to correct or improve it. (सुधारना/संशोधन करना)
◦ Example: The committee decided to amend the constitution to remove the outdated clause.

• "Rectify" means to correct something or make it right, which matches the meaning of "Amend" closely. (सही करना)
◦ Example: The technician worked overnight to rectify the fault in the machine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Harm" (नुकसान पहुँचाना): To cause damage or injury — this is nearly opposite in sense to "Amend".

• Option 3: "Impair" (कमजोर करना): To weaken or damage the quality/function of something — again opposite in sense to improving/correcting.

• Option 4: "Worsen" (बिगाड़ना): To make a situation more bad or serious — the direct opposite of "Amend".

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Amend" with "Emend" (to correct a text) or with the noun "Amends" as in the idiom "to make amends" (to compensate for a wrong done).

• Other synonyms of "Amend" often tested by SSC: reform, revise, improve, correct.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.
Rita will never have changed her job if she would have been promoted.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. would never have.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is a conditional (if-clause) sentence — the "if" clause here reads "if she would have been promoted", which sets up a hypothetical/unreal situation.

• Rule — Conditional Sentences: In sentences that describe a hypothetical or unreal condition, the main (result) clause must use "would", not "will" or "shall", to stay consistent with the conditional ("if") clause.

• Since the "if" clause uses "would have been promoted", the main clause must also use "would": "Rita would never have changed her job..."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No substitution" is incorrect because "will" does not agree with the hypothetical/conditional sense of the sentence; it must be changed.

• Option 2: "should never have" is incorrect because "should" expresses obligation/advisability, not the hypothetical result required by a conditional sentence.

• Option 4: "shall never have" is incorrect for the same reason as "will" — "shall" is a simple-future marker and does not fit a conditional/hypothetical result clause.

NOTE

• In conditional sentences, "will/shall" in the main clause is reserved for real, likely-to-happen (First Conditional) situations, while "would" is used for unreal, hypothetical, or unlikely situations (Second/Third Conditional and mixed conditionals).

• Watch for the auxiliary used in the if-clause — it usually signals which auxiliary (will/would/should/shall) is required in the main clause for consistency.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence.
Sudhir's harrassment is not only perceivable and occasional but also has become a matter of humorous incident before his colleague.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. harrassment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Harassment" — unwanted, persistent behaviour intended to trouble or upset someone. (उत्पीड़न)
◦ Example: The company introduced a strict policy against workplace harassment.

• Spelling key: HAR + ASS + MENT — only ONE "r" and two "s"s. The word printed in the sentence, "harrassment", wrongly doubles the "r".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "colleague" — correctly spelt; means a person one works with. (सहकर्मी)

• Option 3: "Humorous" — correctly spelt; means funny or amusing. (हास्यपूर्ण)

• Option 4: "perceivable" — correctly spelt; means able to be noticed or perceived. (अनुभवगम्य)

NOTE

• Other frequently misspelt double-letter words tested by SSC: occurrence, harass, embarrass, necessary, possession, recommend.

• Trick to remember: "harass" has one "r", two "s"s — think of it as the opposite double-letter pattern of "embarrass" (two r's, two s's).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The trainee wanted to know the________of the course to get a better understanding of the job prospects.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ins and outs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "ins and outs" means all the particular details of something; a complete and thorough knowledge of a subject. (पूरी जानकारी/बारीकियाँ)
◦ Example: She knows the ins and outs of the accounting software after years of using it.

• In the sentence, the trainee wants detailed knowledge of the course to understand job prospects better, which matches "ins and outs" perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "bird's eye view" (सिंहावलोकन): A general overview from above, i.e., a broad, non-detailed view — the opposite of the detailed knowledge implied here.

• Option 3: "crying need": An urgent necessity — this does not fit the context of "wanting to know" something.

• Option 4: "tall talk": Boastful or exaggerated talk — irrelevant to the context of the sentence.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "ins and outs" (detailed knowledge) with "bird's eye view" (general overview) — SSC frequently sets these as confusing distractors in the same question.

• Similar idioms of thorough knowledge: "to know something like the back of one's hand", "at one's fingertips".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
This drama is extremely informative __________ life in Roman times.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. about.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "informative" conventionally takes the preposition "about" when followed by the topic/subject it gives information on.

• Rule — Preposition with "informative": informative about (a topic) = giving useful facts/information regarding that topic.
◦ Example: The documentary is highly informative about marine life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "on" is incorrect — "informative" does not idiomatically pair with "on" in standard usage.

• Option 2: "of" is incorrect — "informative of" is not the accepted collocation.

• Option 4: "for" is incorrect — "for" would suggest purpose/benefit, not the topic being informed about.

NOTE

• Other adjectives that pair with "about": curious about, anxious about, excited about, worried about, passionate about.

• SSC frequently tests fixed preposition collocations with adjectives like this — memorising common adjective + preposition pairs is very useful.

question:
Select the most appropriate collocation to fill in the blank.
Arun and his wife were ______ a baby boy after 18 years of their marriage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. blessed with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The collocation "blessed with" means to be fortunate enough to receive/have something good, and is the standard, natural expression used for having a child, especially after a long wait. (आशीर्वाद स्वरूप प्राप्त होना)
◦ Example: After years of trying, the couple was finally blessed with twins.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "delighted with" is incorrect — this collocation is used for expressing pleasure about something already possessed/experienced, not for describing the event of having a child.

• Option 2: "prepared with" is incorrect — this does not form a natural or meaningful collocation in this context.

• Option 3: "provided with" is incorrect — "provided with" is used for supplying material things/resources, not for the birth of a child.

NOTE

• "Blessed with" is a very commonly tested collocation in SSC exams, typically used with children, talent, good health, or good fortune.

• Compare with other similar collocations: endowed with (talent/quality), gifted with (talent/ability).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Impede
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Hinder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Impede" means to delay or block the progress of something; to obstruct. (बाधा डालना)
◦ Example: Heavy rain impeded the rescue operations.

• "Hinder" means to create difficulty for someone/something, resulting in delay or obstruction, which closely matches "Impede". (रुकावट डालना)
◦ Example: Poor infrastructure hinders economic growth in rural areas.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Intend" (इरादा करना): To have a plan or purpose in mind — unrelated to obstruction.

• Option 2: "Prompt" (प्रेरित करना): To cause or encourage something to happen — nearly opposite, as it aids rather than obstructs.

• Option 3: "Respite" (राहत): A short period of rest or relief — unrelated in meaning to obstruction.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Impede": obstruct, hamper, block, thwart, hold back.

• Antonyms of "Impede" worth remembering: facilitate, assist, expedite.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Poliseman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Policeman" — a male member of the police force. (पुलिसकर्मी)
◦ Example: The policeman directed traffic at the busy junction.

• Spelling key: POLICE + MAN — note the letter "c" (not "s") in "police". The word printed, "Poliseman", wrongly replaces "c" with "s".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Warden" — correctly spelt; a person responsible for supervising a particular place or group. (रक्षक/निगरानीकर्ता)

• Option 3: "Engineer" — correctly spelt; a person who designs/builds machines, structures, etc. (अभियंता)

• Option 4: "Doctor" — correctly spelt; a person qualified to treat people who are ill. (चिकित्सक)

NOTE

• Remember: "police", "policy" and "policing" all take "c", never "s", unlike words such as "advise" (verb) vs. "advice" (noun).

• Other commonly confused occupational-word spellings tested by SSC: Occurrence, Personnel, Secretary, Receptionist.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The audience was mesmerised by the speech delivered by the vivacious lady.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Energetic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Vivacious" means attractively lively and animated in character; full of energy and enthusiasm. (जीवंत/उत्साही)
◦ Example: Her vivacious personality made her the centre of attention at every party.

• "Energetic" means full of energy and enthusiasm, which closely matches the meaning of "vivacious". (ऊर्जावान)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Fearless" (निडर): Having no fear; brave — this describes courage, not liveliness.

• Option 3: "Prosperous" (समृद्ध): Successful in material terms, wealthy — unrelated to liveliness of character.

• Option 4: "Friendly" (मिलनसार): Kind and pleasant towards others — describes sociability, not necessarily energetic liveliness.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Vivacious": lively, spirited, animated, exuberant, sprightly.

• Antonym worth remembering: lethargic, dull, listless.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The gate was opened by the peon.
option_1: The peon is opening the gate.
option_3: The peon was opening the gate.
option_4: The gate was being opened by the peon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The peon opened the gate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The gate was opened by the peon" is in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "the peon" becomes the subject; the past participle "opened" changes to the simple past verb "opened" (V2); and "the gate" becomes the object.
◦ Active: The peon opened the gate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "is opening" is Present Continuous, not Simple Past.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "was opening" is Past Continuous, which describes an ongoing past action, not the simple completed action of the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it is still in the passive voice ("was being opened by"), not active voice, and it also wrongly shifts the tense to Past Continuous passive.

NOTE

• Always identify the exact tense of the passive sentence first (here, Simple Past), and apply only the matching active-voice formula — do not let a distractor with the wrong tense but correct-looking structure mislead you.

• "By + agent" is dropped once the sentence is converted back into the active voice, since the agent becomes the subject itself.

question:
The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. They are on the market already but they are costly.
Q. Their cost depends on the sort you install and the size of your home.
R. These devices extract warmth from the air or the ground, or from water - a bit like a fridge operating in reverse.
S. Climate advisers anticipate that most homes in future will be warmed by heat pumps.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. SRPQ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence S is the ideal opener as it introduces the main topic, "heat pumps", in a general statement: "Climate advisers anticipate that most homes in future will be warmed by heat pumps."

• Sentence R logically follows S, as it explains what these devices (heat pumps, referred to as "these devices") actually do: "These devices extract warmth from the air or the ground..."

• Sentence P follows next, shifting to their current market availability: "They are on the market already but they are costly." — the pronoun "They" naturally refers back to the heat pumps/devices described in R.

• Sentence Q logically concludes the paragraph, elaborating on the cost mentioned in P: "Their cost depends on the sort you install and the size of your home."

• Thus, the coherent order is: S → R → P → Q

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: RQPS is incorrect because it starts with "these devices" (R) without first establishing what the devices are (which S does).

• Option 2: SQRP is incorrect because it jumps from the general introduction (S) directly to cost (Q) before explaining what the devices do (R).

• Option 4: PRSQ is incorrect because it starts with "They are on the market already" (P) without first identifying what "They" refers to.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, first identify the sentence that makes the most natural, topic-introducing opener (often a general statement, as with S here).

• Pay close attention to pronouns ("They", "These", "Their") and linking words — they are the strongest clues to determine the correct sequential order.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The art history teacher was sacked after she were thought taking school supplies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. she was caught.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes a teacher being sacked (dismissed from a job) for a reason related to "taking school supplies" — i.e., taking things without permission (essentially, stealing).

• Rule — Contextual/Collocational Accuracy: The correct verb must both make grammatical sense (subject-verb agreement: "she was", not "she were") and fit the logical context of being caught in the act of wrongdoing.

• "Caught" is the only option that fits both grammatically ("was caught", correct singular agreement) and contextually (being caught taking something is the standard reason for dismissal).

• Corrected sentence: "The art history teacher was sacked after she was caught taking school supplies."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "she was wondered" is incorrect — "wonder" is not used in the passive voice in this way, and it does not logically connect to being sacked.

• Option 2: "she was dumped" is incorrect — "dumped" means abandoned/discarded (usually in a relationship), which is meaningless in this context.

• Option 4: "she was enlightened" is incorrect — "enlightened" means given knowledge or understanding, which does not fit the context of being sacked.

NOTE

• The original underlined portion "were thought" is also grammatically wrong because the singular subject "she" requires "was", not "were".

• "Caught doing something" is a common fixed structure in English meaning "discovered in the act of doing something wrong."

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
Lighting has
P. to become a disrupter and
Q. become human-centric as our
R. requirements change during the day and
S. lighting has to adapt to our change in needs
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. PQRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed opening "Lighting has" naturally connects with P: "to become a disrupter and", forming "Lighting has to become a disrupter and..."

• This is followed by Q: "become human-centric as our", continuing the list of what lighting has to do: "...become human-centric as our..."

• R: "requirements change during the day and" logically completes the "as our..." clause begun in Q: "...as our requirements change during the day and..."

• Finally, S: "lighting has to adapt to our change in needs" completes the sentence with the concluding independent clause joined by "and".

• Full coherent sentence: "Lighting has to become a disrupter and become human-centric as our requirements change during the day and lighting has to adapt to our change in needs."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: PSQR is incorrect because S ("lighting has to adapt...") breaks the flow immediately after P, before the "become human-centric" idea in Q is introduced.

• Option 2: RPQS is incorrect because R ("requirements change...") cannot logically follow "Lighting has" directly — it needs Q's "as our" to precede it.

• Option 3: QRSP is incorrect because Q ("become human-centric as our") cannot directly follow "Lighting has" without P's "to become a disrupter and" first.

NOTE

• In sentence-part rearrangement questions, look for grammatical continuations — an incomplete clause (like "as our...") must be immediately followed by the segment that completes it ("requirements change...").

• Reading the fixed starting phrase carefully (here, "Lighting has") often eliminates one or two options immediately, since only certain segments can grammatically follow it.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Mercy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Clemency.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Mercy" means compassion or forgiveness shown towards someone whom it is within one's power to punish. (दया/क्षमा)
◦ Example: The judge showed mercy and reduced the sentence.

• "Clemency" means mercy, especially shown by someone with authority over an offender, which matches "Mercy" closely. (दयालुता)
◦ Example: The prisoner was granted clemency by the governor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Legacy" (विरासत): Something handed down from a predecessor; unrelated to mercy.

• Option 2: "Clarity" (स्पष्टता): The quality of being clear and easily understood; unrelated to mercy.

• Option 4: "Plurality" (बहुलता): The state of being plural or numerous; unrelated to mercy.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Mercy": compassion, leniency, forgiveness, pity, grace.

• Antonym worth remembering: cruelty, ruthlessness.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
The act of washing oneself
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ablutions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ablutions" is the standard one-word substitute meaning the act of washing oneself, especially as part of a religious ritual or a regular routine. (स्नान/शुद्धिकरण)
◦ Example: He performed his morning ablutions before starting his prayers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Solutions" (समाधान): Answers or means of solving a problem; unrelated to washing.

• Option 3: "Steaming" (भाप देना): Cooking or treating something with steam; unrelated to washing oneself.

• Option 4: "Bathing": While related in general sense, it is simply the common verb for washing the body and is not the specialised one-word-substitution term the question seeks; "Ablutions" is the recognised formal term for this exact phrase in one-word substitution lists.

NOTE

• One-word substitution questions expect the specific, formally recognised term, not a loosely related common word — always prefer the option that is a listed substitution term.

• Other commonly tested one-word substitutions: Soliloquy (talking to oneself), Bibliophile (a lover of books), Misanthrope (a hater of mankind).

question:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
Aryan told me that I knew where to find him.
option_1: Aryan said to me, "You know where to find me."
option_2: Aryan said to me, "You knowing where to find me."
option_3: Aryan said to me, "You are known where to find me."
option_4: Aryan says to me, "You know where to find me."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Aryan said to me, "You know where to find me."

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given reported (indirect) speech sentence uses the reporting verb "told" (Past Tense) and the reported verb "knew" (Past Tense).

• Rule — Converting Indirect to Direct Speech:
◦ The reporting verb "told + object" changes to "said to + object" in direct speech.
◦ The Past Tense verb inside the reported clause ("knew") reverts to the Simple Present Tense ("know") inside the quotation marks, since it represents what was originally said as a general/present fact.
◦ Pronouns are reversed: "I" in indirect speech (referring to the listener, "me") becomes "You" in direct speech; "him" (referring to Aryan, the speaker) becomes "me".

• Applying the rule: "Aryan told me that I knew where to find him" → "Aryan said to me, 'You know where to find me.'"

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because "You knowing" is grammatically wrong — it is not a complete, correctly tensed verb form.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "You are known where to find me" changes the meaning to passive voice and is grammatically incorrect in this context.

• Option 4 is incorrect because the reporting verb is wrongly kept in the Present Tense ("says"), whereas the original indirect sentence uses the Past Tense reporting verb "told", which must be preserved as "said".

NOTE

• When converting reported speech, always check both the reporting verb and the reported verb's tense — a common trap is getting the pronouns right but the tense wrong (as in Option 4) or vice versa.

• Remember the pronoun-reversal rule: pronouns referring to the listener in indirect speech become "you" in direct speech, and pronouns referring to the speaker become "I/me".

question:
Select the idiom that can correctly replace the underlined part of the given sentence.
I know she really wants the promotion, but she really hit me below the hand by telling the boss about my personal problems.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hit me below the belt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to hit someone below the belt" means to treat someone unfairly by doing or saying something hurtful or dishonest, especially something considered outside the accepted rules of decent conduct. (अनुचित तरीके से वार करना)
◦ Example: Bringing up his failed marriage during the debate was really hitting below the belt.

• The expression originates from boxing, where hitting an opponent below the belt (waistline) is illegal and considered a foul, unfair blow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "hit me the bricks" is not a standard idiom; the correct idiom is "hit the bricks" (to start walking/leave), which is unrelated in meaning here.

• Option 2: "hit me below the books" is not a recognised English idiom.

• Option 3: "hit me below the bottle" is not a recognised English idiom.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to unfair treatment: "stab someone in the back" (to betray someone), "play dirty" (to use unfair tactics).

• Do not confuse "hit below the belt" (unfair conduct) with "tighten one's belt" (to spend less money).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
He will make mistakes, but he will learn / by making mistakes. So, dear parents, / once you put the money in your / children's little pockets, forget all on it.
option_1: children's little pockets, forget all on it
option_2: once you put the money in your
option_3: by making mistakes. So, dear parents,
option_4: He will make mistakes, but he will learn
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. children's little pockets, forget all on it.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "forget all on it" uses the wrong preposition; the correct fixed idiomatic expression is "forget (all) about it", not "forget... on it".

• Rule — Fixed Prepositions with Verbs: Certain verbs take a specific, fixed preposition by convention; "forget" (in the sense of no longer thinking/worrying about something) always takes "about".

• Corrected segment: "children's little pockets, forget all about it"

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "once you put the money in your" is grammatically correct.

• Option 3: "by making mistakes. So, dear parents," is grammatically correct.

• Option 4: "He will make mistakes, but he will learn" is grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Commonly tested fixed preposition pairs: forget about, think about, worry about, care about, talk about.

• A frequent SSC error-spotting trap is a wrong or missing preposition in an otherwise fluent-sounding sentence — always check verb-preposition pairs carefully.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Women won their present status through (1)________ and sacrifices rather than through men's kindness. Women and their supporters have fought, and in some places continue to fight for the same rights as (2)________. Laws were made to replace local customs which denigrated and suppressed women's rights. Women have (3)________ higher positions in the world at all levels; political, economic and social. But in reality, women still suffer from (4)________ at various levels. For example, women work more and earn less than men. In addition to that, the majority of the world's poor and illiterate are women. The road to real (5)________ is still long.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. struggle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "and sacrifices", indicating that the missing word must be something that pairs naturally with "sacrifices" as a cause of women's present status.

• "Struggle" means a hard effort to achieve or resist something, and pairs naturally with "sacrifices" to convey the difficult fight women went through.

• Corrected sentence: "Women won their present status through struggle and sacrifices rather than through men's kindness."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "happiness" does not fit — happiness is not something through which status is "won"; it contradicts the idea of hardship implied by "sacrifices".

• Option 3: "dignity" does not fit contextually as the means through which status was won; it is more a result than a method of struggle.

• Option 4: "joy" does not fit for the same reason as "happiness" — it contradicts the hardship implied by the accompanying word "sacrifices".

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the words immediately before and after the blank (here, "through ___ and sacrifices") — they usually indicate the required word's sense (a synonym or logical pair).

• The overall tone of the passage (women's fight for equal rights) should guide word choice throughout all five blanks.

Women and their supporters have fought, and in some places continue to fight for the same rights as (2)________. Laws were made to replace local customs which denigrated and suppressed women's rights. Women have (3)________ higher positions in the world at all levels; political, economic and social. But in reality, women still suffer from (4)________ at various levels. For example, women work more and earn less than men. In addition to that, the majority of the world's poor and illiterate are women. The road to real (5)________ is still long.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. men.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"...continue to fight for the same rights as (2)________." The passage's central theme is women fighting for rights equal to those enjoyed by men**.

• "Men" fits both grammatically and contextually, since the whole passage repeatedly contrasts women's status against that of men (e.g., "rather than through men's kindness", "women work more and earn less than men").

• Corrected sentence: "...continue to fight for the same rights as men."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "everyone" is too vague and does not capture the specific man-woman comparison that is the passage's central theme.

• Option 3: "universal" is grammatically awkward here and does not fit the phrase "the same rights as ________", which needs a noun referring to a group of people, not an adjective.

• Option 4: "politicians" is irrelevant — the passage is about gender equality, not about political figures specifically.

NOTE

• When a cloze passage has a recurring theme (here, women vs. men), later blanks are often best filled by words that continue that same comparison.

• Always re-read the whole passage once fully, since context from a later or earlier sentence often confirms the correct word for a given blank.

Laws were made to replace local customs which denigrated and suppressed women's rights. Women have (3)________ higher positions in the world at all levels; political, economic and social. But in reality, women still suffer from (4)________ at various levels. For example, women work more and earn less than men. In addition to that, the majority of the world's poor and illiterate are women. The road to real (5)________ is still long.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. gained.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"Women have (3)________ higher positions in the world at all levels; political, economic and social."**

• "Gained" means to obtain or achieve something, typically through effort, and is the natural, neutral verb used with "positions" in this achievement-based context.

• Corrected sentence: "Women have gained higher positions in the world at all levels..."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "snatched" carries a negative/forceful connotation (grabbing something suddenly, often unfairly), which does not match the passage's respectful tone about women's achievements.

• Option 2: "gripped" means to hold firmly, which does not collocate naturally with "positions" in this sense.

• Option 3: "plucked" means to pull or pick something out, which is meaningless when applied to "positions".

NOTE

• "Gain a position" is a standard, natural English collocation; always check whether a verb naturally pairs with the following noun (collocational fit), not just its dictionary meaning.

• Words like "snatched" and "gripped", though sometimes near-synonyms of "gained" in isolation, fail collocation tests with certain nouns like "position".

Laws were made to replace local customs which denigrated and suppressed women's rights. Women have (3)________ higher positions in the world at all levels; political, economic and social. But in reality, women still suffer from (4)________ at various levels. For example, women work more and earn less than men. In addition to that, the majority of the world's poor and illiterate are women. The road to real (5)________ is still long.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. discrimination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"But in reality, women still suffer from (4)________ at various levels. For example, women work more and earn less than men."**

• "Discrimination" means unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, and the following example ("women work more and earn less than men") is a textbook illustration of gender discrimination.

• Corrected sentence: "But in reality, women still suffer from discrimination at various levels."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "issues" is too vague and generic; it does not specifically capture the unfair treatment described by the following example.

• Option 2: "tolerance" is a positive quality (acceptance of differences) and does not logically follow "suffer from", which requires a negative noun.

• Option 3: "equality" is also positive and cannot logically be something one "suffers from" — this directly contradicts the sentence's meaning.

NOTE

• The phrase "suffer from" is a strong clue — it must be followed by something negative (a problem, hardship, or injustice), which immediately rules out positive words like "equality" and "tolerance".

• Always check whether the word fits the polarity (positive/negative) demanded by the surrounding sentence structure, not just the general topic.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. equality.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"The road to real (5)________ is still long."** This is the passage's concluding sentence, summarising its central theme.

• The whole passage discusses women's ongoing fight for equal rights and status with men, so the fitting concluding word is "equality" — the ultimate goal the passage describes as "still long" (i.e., not yet fully achieved).

• Corrected sentence: "The road to real equality is still long."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "probability" is meaningless here — "the road to real probability" makes no logical sense in this context.

• Option 2: "maturity" does not connect to the passage's theme of rights and discrimination between men and women.

• Option 4: "eligibility" refers to meeting requirements/qualifications, which is unrelated to the passage's theme of gender equality.

NOTE

• The concluding sentence of a passage often restates or summarises its central theme — always match the final blank to the overall topic discussed throughout, not just the immediate sentence.

• This passage's theme (gender equality) is reinforced by all five blanks together: struggle, men, gained, discrimination, equality — forming one consistent narrative.
